final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and largely reframed the same record more narrowly. That reframing is directionally more accurate: the evidence does support aggregate readiness and rehearsal stability, and the public governance/model-card materials can support monitoring and documentation posture. But the key compliance issue remains unresolved. Under the provided policy, a material limitation affecting a named launch use case must be resolved, disclosed, or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. The admissible record still shows a named shelter-use-case gap, named nonprofit commitments, and an open legal disclosure question, with no evidence of disclosure, resolution, or approved acceptance. That means this is not merely a caveated but otherwise satisfied predicate; the caveat identifies the very compliance condition that remains unmet on the present record. A narrowed certification statement may be more truthful than the original overbroad one, but it is not enough to move the file to compliant_with_caveats on admissible evidence alone.
remaining_concerns: The emergency shelter placement segment still misses target and is named in two nonprofit deployment commitments, so materiality remains live under the policy text.
There is still no admissible evidence that the limitation was resolved before launch.
There is still no admissible evidence that the limitation was disclosed in the required launch documentation.
There is still no admissible evidence of approved pre-launch risk acceptance covering this named launch use case.
Legal review on whether disclosure is required remains open, which leaves the release-policy predicate unresolved.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support operational readiness, but they do not satisfy the separate disclosure-or-acceptance requirement.
